Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be a regular potential with a nonnegative nonincreasing envelope $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, where $R_0<\infty$ and $\int_{R_0}^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr<\infty$. Thus $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ for $|x|_\infty\geq R_0$. For $g>2R_0$ set
$$\eta(g)=g^d\psi(g)+\int_g^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr.$$
Then $\eta(g)\to0$ and
$$\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq 2^{d-1}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Moreover, there is a choice $g(\ell)>0$, for all sufficiently large real $\ell$, such that $g(\ell)\to\infty$, $g(\ell)/\ell\to0$, and
$$\left(\frac{\ell}{g(\ell)}\right)^d\eta(g(\ell))\longrightarrow0.$$
For every fixed finite configuration and all sufficiently large periods $L$, the noncoincident periodic-image tail $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d,\ |k|_\infty\geq K_0}|\phi(x-y+Lk)|$ is absolutely convergent. The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable. This lemma is a deterministic tail estimate; it uses no superstability or thermodynamic-limit conclusion.

Let $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$ be superstable in the splitting convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Suppose $H_{\phi_s}(\omega)\geq-B_sN(\omega)$ and $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta>0$ for $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$, with $\phi_r\geq0$ elsewhere. For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero. This is the cell form used in the continuum pressure arguments.

derivations.claim: Define $m(\rho,e)=\inf\{I(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\Phi(P)\leq e\}$ and $s=-m$. For stationary finite-entropy laws $P,R$, the binary-mixture chain rule on a bounded cube $G$ gives $\theta D(P_G\Vert Q_G)+(1-\theta)D(R_G\Vert Q_G)=D((\theta P+(1-\theta)R)_G\Vert Q_G)+I(S;X_G)$, with $0\leq I(S;X_G)\leq H(S)<\infty$. Divide by $|G|$ and use [F4]; the label entropy vanishes, so $I$ is affine on finite mixtures. The expectation $\rho$ and finite-volume energy expectations are affine, hence their limits $\rho,\Phi$ are affine where finite. Mixtures of feasible laws show $m$ is convex and $s$ concave. If $(\rho_n,e_n)\to(\rho,e)$ and $\liminf m(\rho_n,e_n)<\infty$, choose near-minimizers with bounded $I$. Compactness [F2] gives a convergent subsequence; continuity of $\rho$ by [F6] and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi,I$ in [F1] show the limit is feasible with entropy no greater than the liminf. Thus $m$ is lower semicontinuous and $s$ upper semicontinuous; the same compactness argument attains every finite infimum. For strict feasibility, choose $\rho_1$ in the interior of $D$ below $\nu(\phi)$ with a finite-energy, finite-entropy law $R$. The inequality $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$ gives $\rho_2\in D$ and a finite-entropy law $P$ with $\Phi(P)<e$. If $\rho_2$ is at an endpoint of $D$, mix $P$ with a sufficiently small positive amount of $R$; affinity of $\rho,\Phi,I$ keeps the energy below $e$ and moves the density into the interior of $D$.

For the lower event bound, take a stationary law $P$ with $I(P)<\infty$, $\rho(P)\in D^\circ$, and $\Phi(P)<e$. The cell inequality [F11], stationarity, and $E_PH_{\ell,\mathrm{free}}/\ell^d\to\Phi(P)$ imply a uniform bound on $E_P[T_\ell/\ell^d]$ for large integer $\ell$, hence on $E_P[(N_{\Lambda_\ell}/\ell^d)^2]$. They also give a uniform bound $C$ on $E_P[H_{\ell,\mathrm{free}}^+]/\ell^d$, since the negative part is at most $BN$. Choose $M_j\uparrow\infty$ with $C/M_j\to0$. For each sufficiently large $\ell_j$, let $E_j=\{H_{\ell_j,\mathrm{free}}\leq M_j\ell_j^d\}$ and $p_j=P(E_j)$. Markov's inequality gives $p_j\geq1-C/M_j$. On $E_j$, the cell inequality and $N^2/\ell_j^d\leq T_{\ell_j}$ give $N/\ell_j^d\leq K_j$, where $K_j$ is the positive root bound for $Ax^2-Bx\leq M_j$. The count-density loss under conditioning tends to zero by Cauchy–Schwarz and the uniform second-moment bound. The conditional expected energy density has limsup at most $\Phi(P)$ because the removed energy is positive. The entropy conditioning formula gives $D(P_{\Lambda_{\ell_j}}(\cdot\mid E_j)\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{\ell_j}})\leq\bigl(D(P_{\Lambda_{\ell_j}}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{\ell_j}})+1/\mathrm e_{\rm E}\bigr)/p_j-\log p_j$, where $\mathrm e_{\rm E}$ is Euler's number, so the conditioned block entropy per volume is at most $I(P)+o(1)$. Choose $g_j>2R_0$ with $\eta(g_j)\leq(j^{d+1}K_j^2)^{-1}$ and set $\ell_j=jg_j$, increasing $g_j$ further so $\ell_j$ is large enough for the specific entropy and energy limits above. Then $g_j/\ell_j=1/j\to0$ and $p_j\to1$. In a large periodic cube of side $L$, put $m_L=\lfloor L/(\ell_j+g_j)\rfloor$ cores per coordinate, each of side $\ell_j$, on a periodic grid of exact spacing $a_{L,j}=L/m_L\geq\ell_j+g_j$. Thus every core is separated from every other core and its periodic images by at least $g_j$, and the unoccupied fraction tends to $1-(\ell_j/(\ell_j+g_j))^d$. Put independent conditioned blocks in the cores and leave the complement empty. For two core indices at maximum-norm distance $m\geq1$, the total absolute cross energy per core is at most $C_dK_j^2\ell_j^{2d}\sum_{m\geq1}m^{d-1}\psi(mg_j)$, so its contribution per unit volume is at most $C'_dK_j^2(\ell_j/g_j)^d\eta(g_j)\leq C'_d/j$ by [F10], including the periodic image interactions across the outer boundary. The iid law of core counts and core energies gives the required density and within-core energy laws of large numbers; since the cross-energy error is uniformly bounded by $C'_d/j$, for large fixed $j$ the product block law assigns probability tending to one to $A_L$ as $L\to\infty$, with density in $D$ and energy below $e$ by strict margins. Relative to the Poisson reference on $\Lambda_L$, the product block law has log density equal to the sum of the iid block log densities plus the corridor volume (the Poisson void cost). The block log density is integrable because its relative entropy is finite; truncation followed by the ordinary weak law gives its average limit. Therefore its typical log density per volume is at most $I(P)+o_j(1)$ as $j\to\infty$. On the intersection of $A_L$ with this typical set, changing measure back to $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ gives $Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L)\geq\exp[-L^d(I(P)+o_j(1)+o_L(1))]$. If a minimizing law lies on a constraint boundary, mix it with a strict feasible law; entropy affinity and lower semicontinuity show that the entropy infimum is unchanged. This proves the lower event bound and eventual positivity.

Put $K=\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}:\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}$. The set is closed by [F1], lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$, and continuity of $\rho$ in $\tau_L$. For every configuration with finite $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$, the periodized empirical field satisfies $\rho(R_{L,\omega})=N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d$ by [F7] and $\Phi(R_{L,\omega})=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d$ by Georgii's periodic-energy identity (1994, equation (2.16)); hence $A_L\subseteq\{R_{L,\omega}\in K\}$. The Poisson empirical-field upper bound of [L2], applied to this closed set, gives $$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L)\leq-\inf_{P\in K}I(P)=-m,$$ where $m$ is the minimum in the Statement. Together with step 2.1 this proves the event exponent. The exact periodic empirical field accounts for all long-range image interactions in this upper bound; no fixed empty corridor is used to discard them.

The tangent-plane argument in published [L1] separates the strict-feasibility constraint set in finite dimension [F3]. It supplies a finite $\alpha=\log z$ and a nonnegative coefficient $\beta\ge0$. When $\beta>0$, the constrained entropy minimizers lie in the positive-beta grand variational minimizer set. To spell out the compatible retained-admissibility interpretation when the supporting coefficient is zero, write $m_* =m(D,e)$ and let $(\rho_*,u_*)$ be a contact point. A supporting plane with energy coefficient $\beta=0$ gives $-m(\rho,u)\leq-m_*-\alpha(\rho-\rho_*)$ for every finite-energy pair $(\rho,u)$; equivalently, every stationary finite-energy law satisfies $I(P)-\alpha\rho(P)\geq m_*-\alpha\rho_*$. Equality holds at the constrained minimizers in contact. Any law in $\mathcal K_B$ with finite $I$ is approximated in $\tau_L$ and density by finite-energy separated-block laws $P_j$ with $\limsup_j I(P_j)\leq I(P)$, as constructed in [F9]. Passing the inequality to the limit shows it holds on all of $\mathcal K_B$; equality at a constrained minimizer identifies the same global minimum there. The finite-volume zero-beta weight remains $z^N\mathbf1_{\rm admissible}$ throughout.

Let $U$ be an open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the common grand minimizer set and put $K_U=K\cap U^c$, with $K$ as in step 3.1. The constrained entropy minimum on $K_U$ is strictly larger than $m$: otherwise a sequence with $I\downarrow m$ lies in a compact entropy sublevel [F2], and a limit in the closed set $K_U$ would be a constrained minimizer outside $U$. By [L2],
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}\{R_{L,\omega}\in K_U\}\leq-\inf_{P\in K_U}I(P)<-m.$$
Since $A_L\cap\{R_{L,\omega}\notin U\}\subseteq\{R_{L,\omega}\in K_U\}$, divide this exponential upper bound by the event probability from step 3.1. The conditional empirical fields therefore concentrate in $U$.
For the positive-beta periodic grand law, [L3] gives concentration outside every neighborhood of its zero set, the grand minimizer set. For the retained zero-beta grand law, write its numerator as the Poisson integral of $e^{\alpha N}\mathbf1_{\{R\in\mathcal K_B\cap U^c\}}$ and its denominator as the retained-hard partition. Apply [L2] to the closed set $\mathcal K_B\cap U^c$ with the continuous linear term $-\alpha\rho$; [F9] supplies the denominator rate $-\min_{\mathcal K_B}(I-\alpha\rho)$. Compact entropy levels give a strict gap outside $U$ when the minimizer set is contained in $U$. Thus the zero-beta grand empirical field also concentrates in $U$, using the locally established [F9] and the separate empirical-field bounds; no empirical-field concentration is inferred solely from the printed raw-law theorem. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in both branches.

The conditional law is torus-invariant and its entropy density is $-L^{-d}\log Q_L(A_L)$, which is bounded by the event limit. The matching grand law is torus-invariant as well. At positive beta its entropy density is bounded by the pressure identity, the superstable lower energy bound, and the Poisson entropy count inequality; at zero beta use the same identity with the hard indicator and omit the energy term. Consequently [F8] applies. Its transfer result converts step 5.1 into convergence of the periodically continued laws for every local tame observable under uniqueness. No zero extension outside the fundamental cube is used.

Assume the superstable regular model and Poisson conventions of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], with stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, intensity $\rho$, specific entropy $I$, and energy density $\Phi$ as there defined. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length and define
$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. Define
$$\mathcal K_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}:P\!\left(\left\{\omega:\forall x,y\in\omega,\ x\neq y\Rightarrow x-y\notin B\right\}\right)=1\right\}.$$
For $\beta>0$ put $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$; at $\beta=0$ put $\mathcal M_{0,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$. Then there are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ for which the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}$. If this minimizer set is a singleton, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.
In the $\beta=0$ branch the finite periodic weight is explicitly $z^N$ times the indicator that no displacement between the configuration and any periodic image lies in $B$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

boundaries.evidence: An empty configuration has N=0 and periodic energy zero, and lies in A_L exactly if 0 belongs to D and e>=0. The theorem requires D of positive length and positive box volume; proof2.1 supplies eventual positivity under strict feasibility, without asserting an empty interval has a conditional law.

$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. Define
$$\mathcal K_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}:P\!\left(\left\{\omega:\forall x,y\in\omega,\ x\neq y\Rightarrow x-y\notin B\right\}\right)=1\right\}.$$
For $\beta>0$ put $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$; at $\beta=0$ put $\mathcal M_{0,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$. Then there are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ for which the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}$. If this minimizer set is a singleton, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.
In the $\beta=0$ branch the finite periodic weight is explicitly $z^N$ times the indicator that no displacement between the configuration and any periodic image lies in $B$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

L1.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
L1.source_section: Theorem 4, Section 7, printed pp.177–178 / PDF pp.7–8; complete proof read.
L1.source_statement: For a superstable regular interaction, nondegenerate D with inf D<ν(φ), and e>inf φ(D), the periodic upper-energy event has the stated entropy exponent and common variational minimizers.

risk_review.notes: Read all six proof steps, all twelve suppliers, Georgii Section 7 printed pp.191-194, and Georgii-Zessin Theorem 3.1/Section 5.3 pp.185,199-202. Entropy affinity, energy lsc and compact entropy levels make the constrained entropy cost convex closed and attained; strict feasibility can be moved into the density interior by a finite mixture. Energy-conditioned blocks have deterministic count-density cutoff, finite entropy, strict density/energy margins and periodic exact-spacing gaps; the diagonal gap choice absorbs the growing cutoff. Poisson good-rate upper bound uses exact periodic energy identity, not neglected images. Tangent supporting plane has nonnegative energy multiplier (visually verified beta>=0 on p.177); at zero multiplier, finite-original-energy approximation extends its inequality to the retained-admissible domain. Closed complements of neighborhoods have strict entropy/rate gaps, giving conditional/grand concentration. Torus entropy bounds justify local-tame expectation transfer; upper-energy interval event is kept separate from exact N or a thin shell.

citations.quote: The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below.
The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable.

For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero.

For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.
Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]].

For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$.

Let $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $\beta,z>0$, and $b\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$. On the simple labelled sector $\mathcal S_{L,N}=\{q\in\Lambda_L^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ use $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q)=\sum_{i<j}\phi(q_i-q_j)$ and the periodic energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For $N\geq1$ define
$$Z_b(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_{L,N}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_b(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, and put $\Xi_b(L,z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_b(L,N;\beta)$. The unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ has sector density $e^{-L^d}/N!$ relative to labelled Lebesgue measure, so its normalized grand partition is
$$Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}]=e^{-L^d}\Xi_b(L,z,\beta).$$
The exact-$N$ canonical law $C^b_{L,N}$ has density $e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/(N!Z_b(L,N;\beta))$ on $\mathcal S_{L,N}$, and the grand-canonical law $G^b_{L,z,\beta}$ has density $z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)$ relative to $Q_{\Lambda_L}$. Let $\rho>0$ be an interior attainable density, choose $\alpha=\log z$ supporting the free canonical rate $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, and take $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. Assume
$$L^{-d}\log Z_b(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho).$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
Then for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ there is $c_U>0$ such that
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log C^b_{L,N_L}\{\,\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\,\}\leq-c_U.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$ under $C^b_{L,N_L}$. This is a statement about spatially averaged local observables through the empirical field, not about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

Define its **periodized empirical field**
$$R_{L,\omega}:=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\delta_{T_x\omega^{(L)}}\,dx.$$
The integral is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ under $x\mapsto T_x\omega^{(L)}$.

For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

derivations.claim: For the upper bound, $e^{\alpha N_L}Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\leq\Xi_{\mathrm{per}}(L,e^\alpha,\beta)$ for every real $\alpha$. Divide logarithms by $L^d$, use the free/periodic grand limit [F6], and then take the infimum over $\alpha$. The canonical-grand duality [F5] gives $\limsup L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}\leq F_\beta(\rho)$.

Fix corridor width $k$ larger than the tail cutoff. Restrict the $N_L$ particles to the inner cube of side $L-k$, leaving the corridor empty. The exact-$N_L$ density is still $\rho$. The diagonal-gap supplier [F2] gives the vanishing regular-tail cutoff used here. By [L1], the periodized energy differs from the free inner-cube energy by at most $c_d\delta_kT_{L-k}$. The cell bound [F3] implies $T_{L-k}\leq A^{-1}(H_{L-k}+BN_L)$. Consequently $$ Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\geq e^{-\beta c_d\delta_k BN_L/A}\, Z(L-k,N_L;\beta(1+c_d\delta_k/A)). $$ The canonical theorem [F4] applies at the perturbed inverse temperature, giving the corresponding lower rate.

At fixed interior $\rho$, $F_\beta(\rho)$ is finite and convex as a function of $\beta>0$, by Hölder’s inequality [F8], since each finite-volume log partition is convex and the pointwise limit is finite. A finite convex function is continuous on the open interval: on a compact subinterval, its secant slopes are bounded by the slopes to fixed exterior endpoints. Let $L\to\infty$ in step 1.2 and then $k\to\infty$, so $\delta_k\to0$; continuity yields $\liminf\geq F_\beta(\rho)$.

Step 2.1 established the periodic exact-$N_L$ rate $F_\beta(\rho)$, and [F5] supplies a finite supporting activity. The grand rate in [F6] and the periodized empirical field in [F9] satisfy the hypotheses of [F7] with periodic boundary condition. Hence the periodic empirical fields concentrate near the minimizer set, and concentrate at its singleton when it is unique.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **ultrafilter extension principle** says that every filter on a set is contained in an ultrafilter on that set ([[def-ultrafilter]]).

It is also called the **ultrafilter lemma** and is equivalent over ZF to the Boolean prime ideal theorem, abbreviated BPI. Items below write **assume UL/BPI** precisely when they use this extension principle; they do not thereby assume the full axiom of choice.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Work over ZF. The **real dominated-extension principle**, denoted **HB**, is the following assertion:

For every real vector space $X$, every sublinear functional $p:X\to\mathbb R$ in the sense of [[def-sublinear-functional]], every real linear subspace $M\le X$ in the sense of [[def-linear-subspace]], and every real linear functional $g:M\to\mathbb R$ in the sense of [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]],
$$\bigl(\forall m\in M,\ g(m)\le p(m)\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists F:X\to\mathbb R\ \bigl(F\text{ is real linear},\ F|_M=g,\ \forall x\in X,\ F(x)\le p(x)\bigr).$$

This names an additional principle; it does not assert a proof of HB in ZF. Subsequent results explicitly state when they assume HB. Neither topology nor completeness is part of this assertion. The subspace may be $\{0\}$ or all of $X$. Sublinearity at scalar zero gives $p(0)=0$, and a linear functional has value zero at zero.

Assume the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For integers $N_L$ with $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)$ be the $1/N_L!$-normalized positional partition on the periodized cube, with the image convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in $\tau_L$.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Let $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $C_{L,N_L}$ be the free-boundary positional canonical law with exactly $N_L$ particles, and let $R_{L,\omega}$ be its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. Choose any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$ and set
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$,
$$C_{L,N_L}\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\in U\}\longrightarrow1.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$. This is local observable equivalence for a uniformly sampled bulk location; it makes no claim about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin or about uniqueness for every interaction.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, the specific relative entropy $I(P)$, the intensity $\rho(P)$, and the positional energy density $\Phi(P)=\mathcal E(P)$ defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are established below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

Use the cube $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and the translation $T_x$ defined in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, let $\omega^{(L)}=\{q+Lk:q\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ be its periodic continuation. Define its **periodized empirical field**
$$R_{L,\omega}:=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\delta_{T_x\omega^{(L)}}\,dx.$$
The integral is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ under $x\mapsto T_x\omega^{(L)}$. For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$, define its **empirical-field barycenter** as the probability mixture
$$\bar C_L(B)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(B)$$
for every measurable configuration event $B$. By [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], for a nonnegative measurable test $f$, the mixture identity holds with values in $[0,+\infty]$. For a signed local tame $f$ from [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], the finite expectation formula
$$\bar C_L(f)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(f)=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}E_{C_L}[f(T_x\omega^{(L)})]\,dx$$
is asserted when $\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(|f|)<\infty$. In particular $E_{C_L}N<\infty$ suffices: if a bounded support $A$ is contained in a box of side $a$, then $N_A(T_x\omega^{(L)})\leq (\lceil a/L\rceil+2)^dN(\omega)$ uniformly in $x$. The growth bound $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ therefore gives absolute integrability. For stationary laws write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}\in[0,+\infty]$, with finite intensity meaning $\rho(P)<\infty$; this agrees with the finite-intensity convention in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is a spatial average over the finite box, not the raw finite-volume law viewed at a fixed origin.

For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, and let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Let $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $\beta,z>0$, and $b\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$. On the simple labelled sector $\mathcal S_{L,N}=\{q\in\Lambda_L^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ use $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q)=\sum_{i<j}\phi(q_i-q_j)$ and the periodic energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For $N\geq1$ define
$$Z_b(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_{L,N}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_b(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, and put $\Xi_b(L,z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_b(L,N;\beta)$. The unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ has sector density $e^{-L^d}/N!$ relative to labelled Lebesgue measure, so its normalized grand partition is
$$Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}]=e^{-L^d}\Xi_b(L,z,\beta).$$
The exact-$N$ canonical law $C^b_{L,N}$ has density $e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/(N!Z_b(L,N;\beta))$ on $\mathcal S_{L,N}$, and the grand-canonical law $G^b_{L,z,\beta}$ has density $z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)$ relative to $Q_{\Lambda_L}$. Let $\rho>0$ be an interior attainable density, choose $\alpha=\log z$ supporting the free canonical rate $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, and take $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. Assume
$$L^{-d}\log Z_b(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho).$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For any finite-volume law $C$ and arbitrary event $E$, write $C^*(E)=\inf\{C(A):E\subseteq A,\ A\text{ measurable}\}$ for its outer probability. Here measurability uses the configuration sigma-algebra; on law space the evaluation sigma-algebra is generated by $P\mapsto P(B)$ for measurable configuration events $B$. Convergence in probability in $\tau_L$ means that the outer probability of leaving each open neighborhood tends to zero; for measurable events this is ordinary probability. Then for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ there is $c_U>0$ such that
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log (C^b_{L,N_L})^*\{\,\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\,\}\leq-c_U.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$ under $C^b_{L,N_L}$. This is a statement about spatially averaged local observables through the empirical field, not about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.

derivations.claim: Let $C_L$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law. For $|t|<\beta$, $$ E_{C_L}e^{tH_{\mathrm{per}}} =Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta-t)/Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta). $$ By [F1], the normalized log moment generating function converges to $F_{\beta-t}(\rho)-F_\beta(\rho)$, whose derivative at zero is $e$. For any fixed $\epsilon>0$, choose small positive and negative $t$ so the Chernoff exponents for $H/L^d\geq e+\epsilon$ and $H/L^d\leq e-\epsilon$ are strictly negative. Hence the canonical probability outside the fixed $\epsilon$-window tends to zero.

The supporting activity and singleton minimizer are given. The exact-$N$ periodic rate is [F1]; the choices in [A1], the superstable regular potential, and the empirical-field convention [F4] are precisely the other hypotheses of [F5]. Applying [F5] with periodic boundary gives, for every open $U\ni P_*$, a constant $c_U>0$ with $\limsup L^{-d}\log C_L^*(R_{L,\omega}\notin U)\leq-c_U$. This supplies the exponential estimate needed for the shell comparison.

Choose strictly increasing thresholds $L_k\geq k$ so that for every $L\geq L_k$ the probability outside the $1/k$ window is at most $1/k$. Set $k(L)=\max\{k:L_k\leq L\}$ and $\delta_L=1/k(L)$. Then $\delta_L\downarrow0$ and the canonical probability of the selected shell tends to one. Positivity of the canonical weight on the shell implies positive Poisson reference measure, so the shell law is defined eventually.

Let $U$ be any open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of $P_*$ and let $S_L=\{N=N_L,\ |H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d-e|\leq\delta_L\}$ be the selected shell event. On $S_L$, the unnormalized periodic Boltzmann factor lies between $e^{-\beta L^d(e+\delta_L)}$ and $e^{-\beta L^d(e-\delta_L)}$. For each measurable event, the normalization constants cancel when comparing conditional probabilities; taking infima over measurable supersets gives the same inequality for outer probabilities, so
$$(Q_{\Lambda_L}(\,\cdot\mid S_L))^*(R_{L,\omega}\notin U)\leq\frac{e^{2\beta\delta_L L^d}}{C_L^{\mathrm{per}}(S_L)}\,(C_L^{\mathrm{per}})^*(R_{L,\omega}\notin U).$$
By step 2.1, $C_L^{\mathrm{per}}(S_L)\to1$. By step 1.2, the last outer probability has a strictly negative exponential rate. Since $\delta_L\to0$, the right side tends to zero. Thus the uniform shell empirical field converges in probability to $P_*$.

For any open neighborhood $U$ of $P_*$, choose a basic neighborhood $V$ of $P_*$ contained in $U$, defined by finitely many strict tame-expectation inequalities. It is evaluation-measurable. The free exact-$N$ empirical fields concentrate on $V$ by [F2], so their outer probabilities outside $U$ vanish. The periodic grand empirical fields obey the good LDP [L1]; its unique zero is $P_*$ by [F3], so the measurable-set upper bound outside $V$ has a strictly negative rate by compactness of rate sublevels. As $U^c\subseteq V^c$, its outer probability tends to zero. Together with steps 2.1 and 3.1, this proves the stated three-ensemble conclusion.

## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, and the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], an interior density $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and differentiability of $\beta\mapsto F_\beta(\rho)$ at $\beta>0$. Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For a regular potential and sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. Under this regularity hypothesis, the far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where the tuple notation means $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=H_\phi(\{q_1,\ldots,q_N\})$ when the coordinates are distinct, and $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=+\infty$ on collision diagonals. The integrand is therefore zero on collisions; these diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero by the no-collision construction in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], so this convention leaves all partition integrals unchanged. For $N=0$ the empty tuple has energy zero. Here $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], stationarity means $P\circ T_x^{-1}=P$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$. When $P$ is stationary and $E_PN_{[0,1)^d}<\infty$ (finite intensity), write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D$ defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. If $\phi$ is stable with constant $B$, then $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}\geq-BN_{\Lambda_L}$, so the negative part of $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ is $P$-integrable for every such $P$. Whenever the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
In the variational results below, $\Phi(P)$ denotes this same positional energy density: $\Phi(P):=\mathcal E(P)$. The cited results establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume either limit exists for every stationary finite-intensity law.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary finite-intensity laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B$ has Lebesgue measure zero, the limiting grand law is the unrestricted activity-$z$ Poisson law. If $|B|>0$, that Poisson law is not in $\mathcal K_B$, so no limiting minimizer is that law. Nonemptiness alone is insufficient: $B=\{0\}$ forbids no pair of distinct points. The retained branch never assigns a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces. For $E \in \mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$, define

$$(\mu \times \nu)(E) := \int_X \nu(E_x)\,d\mu = \int_Y \mu(E^y)\,d\nu.$$

The two displayed integrals are well-defined by
[[prop-sigma-finite-section-measure-functions-are-measurable]] and equal by
[[thm-iterated-section-measures-agree-on-product-measurable-sets]]. This is the
**product measure** of $\mu$ and $\nu$.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $a_i \le b_i$ be reals for $i<n$. Write

$$R^{\circ} := \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i < x_i < b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}, \qquad \overline{R} := [a,b] = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i \le x_i \le b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}$$

([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]). Then $R^{\circ}$ is open and
$\overline{R}$ is closed, so both are Borel and Lebesgue measurable, and **every**
set $R$ with $R^{\circ} \subseteq R \subseteq \overline{R}$ is Lebesgue
measurable with

$$\lambda_n(R) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}(b_i-a_i).$$

In particular this covers the four one-dimensional face conventions in each
coordinate — the open box, the closed box $[a,b]$, the half-open box
$B(a,b) = \prod_{i<n}(a_i,b_i]$ of [[def-half-open-box]], and every mixture of
them, in any combination of coordinates — and it gives measure $0$ to all of them
whenever $a_i = b_i$ for some $i<n$. For a half-open box with infinite
parameters the value is already
$\lambda_n(B) = \operatorname{vol}(B)$ ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]).

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces. Then:

1. the set function $E \mapsto (\mu \times \nu)(E)$ of
   [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]] is a measure on
   $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$;
2. for measurable rectangles,
   $$(\mu \times \nu)(A \times B)=\mu(A)\nu(B),$$
   with the nonnegative extended-product convention $0\cdot\infty=\infty\cdot0=0$;
3. the measure $\mu \times \nu$ is sigma-finite; and
4. it is the unique measure on $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$ with the
   rectangle formula.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

**The factorial.** By the recursion theorem ([[thm-recursion]]) applied to the
set $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$, the starting element $(0,1)$ and the function
$f(k, v) = (\sigma(k),\, v \cdot \sigma(k))$, and by the same induction on the
first coordinate as in [[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]], there is a unique
$F : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with

$$F(0) = 1, \qquad F(\sigma(n)) = F(n)\cdot\sigma(n) \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

We write $n! := F(n)$. Thus $0! = 1$, $1! = 0!\cdot 1 = 1$, $2! = 1!\cdot 2 = 2$,
$3! = 6$, $4! = 24$, $5! = 120$, $6! = 720$.

**$0! = 1$ is the base clause of this recursion**, not a convention imported from
elsewhere. Nothing about empty products is presupposed; the agreement with the
empty product is proved below, in clause (a), rather than assumed.

**Truncated difference.** Throughout, $n - k$ is the operation fixed in
[[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]]: the unique $j$ with $k + j = n$ when
$k \le n$, and $0$ when $n < k$.

**The falling factorial.** For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ define $n^{\underline{k}}$ by
recursion on $k$, by the recursion theorem applied to
$\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ with starting element $(0,1)$ and
$f(k, v) = (\sigma(k),\, v \cdot (n-k))$:

$$n^{\underline{0}} = 1, \qquad n^{\underline{\sigma(k)}} = n^{\underline{k}}\cdot(n-k) .$$

So $n^{\underline{1}} = 1\cdot(n-0) = n$ and $n^{\underline{2}} = n\,(n-1)$, and
for $k \le n$ the value is the product $n(n-1)\cdots(n-k+1)$ of the $k$ topmost
factors.

**Four facts, proved here because the page uses each of them.**

**(a) The factorial is the product of the first $n$ positive naturals.**
$n! = \prod_{j<n}\sigma(j) = \prod_{j<n}(j+1)$, the $\mathbb{N}$-valued product of
[[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]]. Induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]): at
$n = 0$ both sides are $1$, the empty product and the base clause agreeing; and
$\prod_{j<\sigma(n)}\sigma(j) = \big(\prod_{j<n}\sigma(j)\big)\cdot\sigma(n) = n!\cdot\sigma(n) = \sigma(n)!$.
**So the empty-product reading and the base-clause reading are the same reading**,
and neither was assumed.

**(b) $n! \ne 0$, and $\iota(n!) = \prod^{\mathbb{R}}_{j<n}\iota(j+1)$.** For the
first, $0! = 1 \ne 0$ ([[thm-omega-is-peano-system]]) and
$\sigma(n)! = n!\cdot\sigma(n)$ is a product of two nonzero naturals, which is
nonzero: if $xy = 0$ with $y \ne 0$ then $xy = 0\cdot y$
([[lem-nat-mult-identity]]) and cancellation gives $x = 0$
([[lem-nat-mult-cancellative]]). So $n! \ne 0$ for every $n$ by induction. For the second, apply the bridge clause
6 of that lemma to clause (a) above. This is what makes the factorial of this
page and the real-valued product $\prod_{j<n}(j+1)$ used elsewhere in the library
**one object seen twice**, rather than two unrelated notions.

**(c) $n^{\underline{k}}\cdot(n-k)! = n!$ for $k \le n$.** Induction on $k$, for
all $n$ at once. At $k = 0$ this reads $1 \cdot n! = n!$. Assume it at $k$ and
let $\sigma(k) \le n$; then $k \le n$, and writing $d := n - k$ we have
$k + d = n$ and $d \ne 0$, since $k + 0 = k \ne n$; so $d = \sigma(e)$ for a
unique $e$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]), and $\sigma(k) + e = n$, that is
$e = n - \sigma(k)$ ([[lem-nat-add-cancellative]]). Therefore
$n^{\underline{\sigma(k)}}\cdot\big(n-\sigma(k)\big)! = n^{\underline{k}}\cdot(n-k)\cdot e! = n^{\underline{k}}\cdot\big(e!\cdot\sigma(e)\big) = n^{\underline{k}}\cdot\sigma(e)! = n^{\underline{k}}\cdot(n-k)! = n!$,
using commutativity and associativity of multiplication
([[lem-nat-mult-associative]], [[lem-nat-mult-commutative]]) and the recursion
clause for the factorial.

**(d) Boundary values.** $n^{\underline{0}} = 1$ for every $n$, by the base
clause; $n^{\underline{n}} = n!$, since clause (c) at $k = n$ gives
$n^{\underline{n}}\cdot 0! = n!$ and $0! = 1$; and
$n^{\underline{k}} = 0$ whenever $k > n$. For the last, $n - n = 0$ gives
$n^{\underline{\sigma(n)}} = n^{\underline{n}}\cdot 0 = 0$, the clause
$x \cdot 0 = 0$ being definitional ([[def-nat-multiplication]]), and if
$n^{\underline{k}} = 0$ then
$n^{\underline{\sigma(k)}} = 0$ as well, so $n^{\underline{k}} = 0$ for every
$k \ge \sigma(n)$ by induction.

derivations.claim: On the ordered region $x_1<x_2$, allowed pairs satisfy $x_2\geq x_1+a$, so their volume is $\int_0^{L-a}(L-x_1-a)\,dx_1=(L-a)^2/2$. The coordinate-swap map preserves product Lebesgue measure, so the region $x_2<x_1$ has the same volume; the diagonal has zero product measure. Thus the full labeled allowed volume is $(L-a)^2$, and division by $2!$ gives $Z(L,2;0)=(L-a)^2/2$.
Since $0<a<L$, $(L-a)^2/2<L^2/2$, the unrestricted ideal-gas two-particle canonical term. The strict deficit is caused by the forbidden separation band and remains at beta zero by [F2].

## Example

In one spatial dimension, let $\phi(x)=+\infty$ for $|x|<a$ and $0$ otherwise, with $a>0$. On an interval $[0,L]$, define the beta-zero weight by retaining the forbidden-pair exclusion as in [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]]. If $L>a$, the two-particle canonical partition is
$$Z(L,2;0)=\frac{(L-a)^2}{2},$$
while the unrestricted ideal-gas value is $L^2/2$. Thus the retained hard-core beta-zero ensemble is not the Poisson ideal gas.

derivations.claim: Order the coordinates $0\leq x_1<\cdots<x_N\leq L$. The exclusion constraints are $x_{i+1}-x_i\geq a$. Apply the coordinatewise translation $x_i\mapsto y_i=x_i-(i-1)a$; each one-coordinate translation preserves Lebesgue measure [F5], so product measure is preserved. The ordered region becomes $0\leq y_1\leq\cdots\leq y_N\leq S$, where $S=L-(N-1)a$. The cube $[0,S]^N$ splits, up to equality sets of zero product measure, into $N!$ coordinate-order regions. Product-measure uniqueness makes these permutation chambers equal in measure, so the ordered region has volume $S^N/N!$. The full labeled allowed volume is $N!$ times this, and canonical division by $N!$ gives $Z(L,N;\beta)=S^N/N!$.

If $L=(N-1)a$, then $S=0$ and the transformed region is a null set; its integral is zero. If $L>(N-1)a$, then $S>0$ and the ordered region has positive product volume. Thus the maximal-density endpoint does not carry a positive canonical partition at exact close packing; the interior-only theorem [F2] makes no contrary assertion.

In one dimension, let the pair potential be infinite when the separation is less than $a>0$, and zero otherwise. For $N\geq1$ labeled rods in $[0,L]$, with canonical positional normalization $1/N!$, write $S=L-(N-1)a$. If $S>0$, translating the ordered coordinates by $y_i=x_i-(i-1)a$ gives
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac{S^N}{N!}=\frac{(L-(N-1)a)^N}{N!},\qquad \beta>0.$$
If $S=0$, the allowed configuration set has zero Lebesgue measure and $Z(L,N;\beta)=0$. Along $N\to\infty$ with $L=(N-1)a$, the density $N/L\to1/a$ while every finite-volume partition is zero. Thus the thermodynamic close-packing endpoint is approached by a sequence of zero-weight finite systems; it is not realized by a positive canonical partition. The interior canonical limit theorem makes no assertion at that endpoint.

In one dimension, let the pair potential be infinite when the separation is less than $a>0$, and zero otherwise. For $N\geq1$ labeled rods in $[0,L]$, with canonical positional normalization $1/N!$, write $S=L-(N-1)a$. If $S>0$, translating the ordered coordinates by $y_i=x_i-(i-1)a$ gives
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac{S^N}{N!}=\frac{(L-(N-1)a)^N}{N!},\qquad \beta>0.$$
If $S=0$, the allowed configuration set has zero Lebesgue measure and $Z(L,N;\beta)=0$. Along $N\to\infty$ with $L=(N-1)a$, the density $N/L\to1/a$ while every finite-volume partition is zero. Thus the thermodynamic close-packing endpoint is approached by a sequence of zero-weight finite systems; it is not realized by a positive canonical partition. The interior canonical limit theorem makes no assertion at that endpoint.

risk_review.notes: Read both verification steps and all eight suppliers. Ordered hard rods translate to 0<=y1<=...<=yN<=S; product translation and permutation invariance give S^N/N!, including N=1. S=0 is a singleton/null region in R^N; exact close-packing sequence uses N->infinity (N>=2 for positive L) and density tends 1/a. S>0 is positive. No canonical theorem at endpoints is claimed.

citations.quote:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, the specific relative entropy $I(P)$, the intensity $\rho(P)$, and the positional energy density $\Phi(P)=\mathcal E(P)$ defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are established below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.
This is an information functional relative to the specified unit-intensity Poisson law; changing the reference changes its value.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.
Equivalently, a net $(P_\alpha)$ converges to $P$ in $\tau_L$ exactly when $E_{P_\alpha}f\to E_Pf$ for every measurable local $f$ with at most linear growth in the count of a bounded support.

derivations.claim: Let $P,R$ be stationary laws of finite specific entropy and let $P_\theta=\theta P+(1-\theta)R$. For a bounded cube $G$, the binary-label chain rule [F3] gives $$ \theta D(P_G\Vert Q_G)+(1-\theta)D(R_G\Vert Q_G) =D((P_\theta)_G\Vert Q_G)+I(S;X_G), $$ where $S$ is the mixture label and $X_G$ the observed configuration. Since $0\leq I(S;X_G)\leq H(S)<\infty$, divide by $|G|$ and take the cube limit [F2]; $H(S)/|G|\to0$, so $I(P_\theta)=\theta I(P)+(1-\theta)I(R)$. The expectation defining $\rho$ is affine. For finite energy densities, $E_{P_\theta}H_G=\theta E_PH_G+(1-\theta)E_RH_G$ for every $G$; dividing by volume and taking limits gives affinity of $\Phi$. Thus $J$ is affine on finite mixtures of finite-$J$ laws.

Applying step 1.1 to $P_0,P_1$ gives $J(P_\theta)=\theta J(P_0)+(1-\theta)J(P_1)=m$, so every mixture is a minimizer. Put $P_{2n}=P_0$ and $P_{2n+1}=P_1$. The even and odd subsequences converge locally to $P_0$ and $P_1$. Since distinct laws differ on a bounded-region measurable event, its indicator is a bounded local test by [F4] with different expectations; the full sequence therefore has no $\tau_L$ limit. Both accumulation points are minimizers.

boundaries.reason: Suppose $J(P)=I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z$ has two distinct stationary minimizers $P_0\ne P_1$ with equal finite value $m$. Boundary empty: The Statement has no empty-configuration branch; its claim concerns the displayed positive-volume, density, or conditional regime.

case_scope.source_excerpt: Suppose $J(P)=I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z$ has two distinct stationary minimizers $P_0\ne P_1$ with equal finite value $m$. Every finite mixture $P_\theta=\theta P_0+(1-\theta)P_1$, $0\leq\theta\leq1$, also minimizes $J$. The sequence of stationary laws alternating between $P_0$ and $P_1$ has two distinct local accumulation points and does not converge. This conditional mathematical example shows why compactness alone yields minimizer-set accumulation; it does not assert a finite-volume ensemble realizes the sequence or that a particular continuum potential exhibits coexistence.
